newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile central bank sees new rates cut if economy steady.
newsitem.headline: Chile central bank sees new rates cut if economy steady.

text.p: Chile's Central Bank, which cut interest rates Thursday, will loosen its tight credit policy further provided economic growth and inflation continue in line with forecasts, said a top bank official.
"If the economic indicators continue to be on track, then certainly there will be an easing of rates," said the bank's research director Nicolas Eyzaguirre.
The bank trimmed its daily interbank rate by 0.25 percentage point to 7.25 percent, the first easing in its year-old restrictive monetary policy.
The rate cut is a clear sign that the bank is confident Chile's economic growth has been brought under control and that inflation is falling, said Eyzaquirre.
"The measure is a clear signal in terms of expectations. We are in a descending curve (of growth) and we believe that the normalization of growth and rates has started," he said.
Acting Finance Minister Manuel Marfan said Friday the government expects growth to be at its slackest in the first quarter of the year with the economy expanding under four percent.

The economy expanded around seven percent in 1996 with growth slowing steadily in the last few months. The economy expanded close to 10 percent in the first quarter of 1996 which prompted the bank to hike rates in April.
